_meta.rule: An entry requires BOTH a `verification` (what outside the instrument it agrees with) and a `falsification` (the measurement that would have shown it wrong, and its outcome). Inputs -- material properties, physical constants, requirements -- carry `source` instead, and are marked kind=input. Results carry kind=result. error:null means UNMEASURED, never zero.

_meta.indirection: A NAME ALONE MUST NOT RESOLVE. Entries with a `contexts` list hold several recorded values discriminated by context (solver, mesh, extraction, ne, ...). values.get(name, **context) returns one or REFUSES, printing the alternatives. Added 2026-08-25 after CONVENTIONS 7aq/7at: every serious error in that window was one name meaning different measured things in different contexts. Legacy single-value entries (no `contexts`) still resolve.

torch.sapphire.permittivity.material: single-crystal sapphire (Al2O3), eps PERPENDICULAR to the c-axis
torch.sapphire.permittivity.source: ⚠️ RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-25 by recovering the original work from git: `git show 2db1d59^:experiments/waveguide/FINDINGS.md` line 4580, 'R32 ✅ and R33 ✅: sapphire is buildable'. R32 IS external empirical work and it DOES carry forward — but it answers ORIENTATION, not the SCALAR. It measured c-longitudinal vs c-transverse (f 2.4053 -> 2.4064, +1.1 MHz; CV shift 0.0006 against 0.535 for a full m=2 = 0.11% of it) and concluded 'c-axis longitudinal' is PREFERRED, NOT REQUIRED, because the torch holds too little field for a 23% anisotropy to matter. It TOOK eps = 11.6 as given.
torch.sapphire.permittivity.note: 🔴 THE AXIS ASSIGNMENT IS EXPLICIT AND CONTRADICTS THE STANDARD CONVENTION. geometry.py:1416-1419 (from R98) states: 'eps_PERP_c = 11.6 — what E_phi sees with the c-axis longitudinal; 9.4 is eps_PARALLEL_c'. The standard microwave convention for uniaxial alpha-Al2O3 is the REVERSE: eps_PAR_c (extraordinary) ~11.5-11.6, eps_PERP_c (ordinary) ~9.3-9.4. ⚠️ R32 CANNOT ARBITRATE — 'c-longitudinal reproduces isotropic 11.6 exactly' confirms the simulation put 11.6 on the perpendicular axis, which is the assumption under test. CIRCULAR. 🔢 IF THE STANDARD IS RIGHT: TE011's E_phi is azimuthal, so with c along the tube axis E_phi is PERPENDICULAR to c and sees 9.4, not 11.6. At the local slope of -6.56 MHz per unit eps that is +14.4 MHz against a measured total torch shift of -13.87 MHz — IT LARGELY CANCELS. ✅ CLOSES WITH: one sapphire datasheet giving eps along and across c. No solve needed to decide it; a solve only confirms the consequence.

wall.conductivity.s_per_m.source: R58 adopted bare electropolished aluminium on OPTICAL grounds (no plating to degrade or flake into the optical path). The conductivity is the handbook value for 6061 at 20 C, not a measurement of our surface — a real electropolished wall will fall SHORT of it, so every Q computed from this is an UPPER bound.
wall.conductivity.s_per_m.note: Declared here because this programme's baselines start empty by design and nothing is inherited without re-derivation. The MATERIAL CHOICE is inherited from R58 and still needs its own re-derivation (optical vs Q trade); the NUMBER is a handbook input, which is why kind=input and it carries source rather than verification/falsification.
